"MAX-A-MILLION" can match another game on price and top prize and still pay out very differently. This game is a game that pays many small prizes and few large ones. Of its unclaimed prize money, most is in wins under $5,000 and the rest is in bigger prizes. Neither kind is better, and each suits different players.

If "MAX-A-MILLION" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
985.headline: Where the prize money is

988.body:
About two-thirds of the tickets for "Emerald 10's" have been sold. The game is in the second half of its run. The key question is whether the tickets or the top prizes run out first. Right now, the top prizes are being claimed more slowly than the tickets are selling, which is a good sign.

Every line of Emerald 10's's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.

994.headline: Early stage or late

995.body:

995.headline: How far along this game is

996.body:
The most common win left on "$1,000,000 Triple Play" is $20. The second biggest prize left is $50,000, and two of those are still unclaimed. The prize table is what defines a scratcher, and this page counts every level of it.

Everything above about "$1,000,000 Triple Play" comes from the North Carolina Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
